item.title: Booking a Shared Sports Hall
item.description: Arrange practice sessions in a shared sports hall and follow the rules for using the space and equipment.

children.definition: A form or message asking staff to hold a space for your group at a particular time.
children.example: Please include the number of people in your reservation request so staff can offer you the right space.

children.definition: A period of organised activity that takes place once every week.
children.example: We asked for a weekly session on Tuesday evenings so everyone could come after work.
collocations: move a weekly session to Mondays

children.definition: Stripes on a sports hall floor that show the edges and other parts of an area used for play.
children.example: Use the blue line markings for our practice tonight because the yellow ones are for a different game.

children.definition: The bottoms of shoes that are free of dirt or mud.
children.example: Bring a pair with clean soles and put them on before you step into the hall.
collocations: make sure your shoes have clean soles

children.definition: A service that lets you pay to use items for a short time and give them back afterwards.
children.example: Ask about equipment hire when you arrange your practice if you need a net for the evening.

children.definition: A large piece of hanging material used to split a room into separate areas.
children.example: Ask the supervisor to lower the divider curtain so both groups can practise at the same time.

children.definition: Agreement from someone in charge that you can do something.
children.example: You need permission from the hall supervisor before you move the benches into the corridor.

children.definition: To get everyone and everything your group brought out of the space so others can use it.
children.example: Please clear the hall by eight because the next group needs the full space.
collocations: clear the hall before the next session

children.definition: To continue past the planned finishing time.
children.example: We can start with a shorter warm-up so our practice doesn't run over into the next group's session.
collocations: run over into the next session

children.definition: A piece of furniture or a space with doors where things are kept.
children.example: Put the mats in the cupboard beside the hall entrance when your group finishes.
collocations: put the mats in the cupboard

children.definition: The largest number of people a place can safely hold.
children.example: With both groups practising together, we'll be close to the hall's capacity of forty people.

children.definition: An arrangement in which more than one group can use the same space.
children.example: The hall is set aside for shared use on Thursday evenings, so our group will have only one side of it.

children.definition: To say that an arrangement is definite and can go ahead.
children.example: Could you confirm our reservation for Friday so I can tell the group where to meet?

children.definition: To tell someone officially ahead of time that you plan to end or cancel an arrangement.
children.example: If your group can't use the hall on Friday, please give notice by Wednesday so staff can offer the space to another group.
collocations: give notice at least two days before practice
